pages.title: Strait of Hormuz — US withdraws 20% transit fee

facts.text: US President Donald Trump proposed a 20% reimbursement fee on cargo through Strait of Hormuz ("Guardian of the Hormuz Strait") — withdrawn one day later, replaced by trade/investment deals with Gulf countries
facts.head: What happened

facts.text: IMO opposed — no legal basis for tolls on international strait transit
facts.head: What happened

facts.text: ⚠ Neither US nor Iran has ratified UNCLOS — but transit passage is customary law; tolls apply to artificial canals (Suez, Panama)
facts.head: What happened

facts.text: Iran's FM called 20% excessive
facts.head: What happened

facts.text: Conflict began: February 2026; Iran asserted sovereignty, temporarily closed Strait
facts.head: US–Iran context

facts.text: Interim US–Iran pact: June 17, 2026 — transits crossed 90 on June 24; avg 40–50/day vs pre-war up to 140
facts.head: US–Iran context

facts.text: Hormuz: between Iran and Oman; links Persian Gulf with Gulf of Oman; nearly one-fifth of global oil and LNG
facts.head: US–Iran context

facts.text: Item via Hormuz: Crude oil imports; Share: about 40%
facts.head: India's exposure

facts.text: Item via Hormuz: LNG imports; Share: about 60%
facts.head: India's exposure

facts.text: Item via Hormuz: LPG imports; Share: about 90%
facts.head: India's exposure

facts.text: Import dependence: crude 88%+; LPG 60%; natural gas about 50%
facts.head: India's exposure

facts.text: India imports 1.8–2 billion barrels/yr; every USD 1/barrel adds up to USD 2 billion
facts.head: India's exposure

facts.text: Fee could have added about USD 9 billion/yr
facts.head: India's exposure

facts.text: Oil imports March–May 2026: up 47% to USD 48.88 billion
facts.head: India's exposure
